questions.history: Set delay to 5 ms and jitter to 20 ms.
questions.prediction: The parent passes a factor of 4 to Reactor and can reject the policy at subscription. The merge should recover "ok" on the second target subscription without a jitter configuration error.
questions.basis: Four exceeds Reactor’s jitter-factor upper bound of one. The upstream Flux/Mono fixtures check attempts and final exceptions.
questions.refutation: On the merge the subscriber sees a jitter error, the operation does not recover, or the attempt count differs from two.

questions.history: Use 10 ms delay, 5 ms jitter, and a target whose cold publisher succeeds immediately.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should produce "ok" with one subscription to the target.
questions.basis: Both conversions give a factor of 0.5. An initial success requires no retry.
questions.refutation: The successful value disappears or the target is resubscribed.

questions.history: Compare two otherwise identical first-attempt successes on the merge. Keep the base delay at 5 ms and vary only jitter from 20 ms to Duration.ofDays(107000).
questions.prediction: Clamping predicts the same successful result and one subscription. The landed arithmetic predicts that the large option overflows toNanos() during adaptation, before any subscription.
questions.basis: Both jitter values already exceed the base delay. The larger is representable as a Duration and in milliseconds, while 107000 × 86400 × 10⁹ exceeds Long.MAX_VALUE. No retry or long wait is needed.
questions.refutation: A synchronous ArithmeticException and zero target subscriptions for the larger input refute preservation. Successful readback from both refutes the overflow prediction for this public path.
